_comment: Tolerated SKIP REASONS, keyed on the string `ailang test --format json`
puts in a skipped test's `error` field. Never keyed on a filename: any
file may hit any of these, and a file list would need editing every time
one did, which is the hand-maintained roster tools/test_coverage exists to
avoid. A skip whose reason matches no record here is red (unrecorded_skip),
so a new kind of silently-unrun test cannot arrive quietly.
`expected: always` means the reason must appear somewhere in every run --
if it stops appearing, either upstream implemented the feature and the
tests should be switched back on, or the tests were deleted, and both are
worth a red (stale_skip_record). `expected: sometimes` means the reason is
non-deterministic and a run without it is reported, never failed on: a
flaky gate gets relaxed, and a relaxed inventory is worthless.
Matching is by PREFIX because both reasons below carry variable tails

records.prefix: Named test blocks not yet implemented
why: AILANG v0.26.0 parses `test "name" { ... }` blocks and then skips
every one of them, while the runner prints `All tests passed!` and
exits 0. src/core/prompts_test.ail carries six tests in this form and
all six are dead: `6 tests: 0 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped`.
This is the vacuity shape the exit status cannot express, and it is
why every rule in derive.py reads a number rather than a return code.
disposition: Not fixable in this repo on this pin. The tests are correct and will
start running when upstream implements the form; the `always` marking
means the day that happens, this record goes stale and the inventory
says so rather than leaving six tests quietly passing without running.
Filed against the pin rather than worked around: rewriting the six as
`tests [...]` blocks would restore the coverage but would also hide
that the form is unimplemented from every other file that uses it.

why: AILANG's property generator covers primitives only. A `requires`
contract on a function taking an `Option[string]` or a user-declared
ADT generates a property it cannot then feed, so the property is
skipped. src/core/tool_runtime.ail loses two this way -- `isSome` on
`Option[string]` and `is_native_backend` on `ToolBackend`.
This record exists because the inventory found it. It is a third skip
class, distinct from the two below and above, and neither the item's
handoff nor its measurement knew about it: the file reads `12 passed,
0 failed` and exits 0, so nothing before today could see the two
properties that never ran.
disposition: Not fixable on this pin without deleting the contracts, which would
trade a silent gap for a real loss. Marked `always` so the day AILANG
grows ADT generators this record goes stale and the inventory says
so, rather than leaving two properties quietly not running.

records.prefix: requires not satisfied by random input
why: A `requires` contract makes AILANG generate a property test. When the
generator cannot produce input satisfying the precondition it gives up
and reports a skip. src/core/compress.ail loses two properties this
way -- `truncate_with_suffix` and `compress_output` both require
`max_chars >= 0` and the generator keeps drawing negative ints.
The property is not wrong; the generator is untargeted. The coverage
is nonetheless lost, and the loss was invisible before this inventory
because the runner calls the file green.
disposition: A real gap and a real finding, owned by whoever next touches
compress.ail's contracts: tighten the generator or narrow the input
type so the precondition is reachable.
Marked `sometimes` rather than `always` because it depends on drawn
input: a run whose draws happen to satisfy the precondition reports no
skip at all, and failing on that absence would make this gate flaky.
Cluster 13's fb_2ad074d754cd2c25 is the precedent -- a flaky gate gets
worked around, and a worked-around gate stops being read.
